name: light-table
title: Light Table
description: A binary inspector rendered as an offset gutter, a hex pane and an ASCII pane on a light table. Hovering or focusing any byte cell registers the matching cell across panes with a foreground tint and a hairline rule drawn across the seam between them, so hex and ASCII resolve to the same byte instead of two disconnected dumps.
useWhen: inspecting raw bytes — a file header, a wire payload, a binary blob — where hex and ASCII need to read as one registered object rather than two separate dumps; hovering or focusing a byte cell bridges both panes and a live footer decodes the selected byte range as uint16/uint32/UTF-8. Pick log-viewer-ascii-tail for line-oriented log text and diff-unified-viewer for line-level change comparison — neither operates on bytes, and neither has a cross-pane registration mechanic to bridge.
instruction: Build <LightTable bytes bytesPerRow title className> over a byte array (default a 64-byte plausible PNG-header fragment chosen so every value class already appears at rest: the 0x89 signature byte is high-bit, 'PNG'/'IHDR'/'tEXt' are printable, CR/LF/SUB/NUL are control/null). Three-column CSS layout in Geist Mono: an offset gutter (one row label per 16-byte row, e.g. '0x0010'), a hex pane (role=grid, one button per byte, 16 per row), a thin inter-pane seam, then an ASCII pane (aria-hidden, mirrors the hex grid's information so it never duplicates it for assistive tech) — thin --border rules separate every column. MECHANIC: hovering (pointerenter) or focusing any byte cell in either the hex or ASCII pane sets one shared 'live index'; whichever cell (hex or ASCII) currently holds that index gets an inline style background of exactly color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 8%, transparent) — never a Tailwind opacity utility for this specific tint, the literal CSS function is the point — and an absolutely positioned 1px rule (data-bridge-rule) is drawn across the seam column, overhanging slightly into both panes, at that row's vertical center — only rendered when a live index exists, so nothing crosses the seam at rest. The live index is hoverIndex when the pointer is over a cell, else focusedIndex when the hex grid currently holds DOM focus, else null — so resting between interactions shows no tint and no seam rule, and byte structure is legible purely from the value-class ramp. VALUE-CLASS RAMP: every hex and ASCII cell carries a data-value-class attribute (null/control/highbit/printable) driving both its text color and, in the ASCII pane, its glyph — 0x00 renders '·', 0x01-0x1F and 0x7F render '▖', 0x80-0xFF render '▓', printable bytes render their real character — so non-printable structure reads before any interaction, not as a uniform dot. SELECTION: focusedIndex is a roving-tabindex active cell (tabIndex 0 only on the current cell) that Shift-drag (pointerdown with shiftKey sets the anchor to the prior focusedIndex if none exists yet and starts a drag; subsequent pointerenter while dragging keeps moving focusedIndex) or Shift+ArrowKey (preventDefault; anchor set to focusedIndex before the move if none exists, then focusedIndex moves) extends into a contiguous byte range; a bare click or plain ArrowKey clears the anchor and collapses to a single cell. Selected cells get the same color-mix background at a stronger 14% mix, applied identically to both panes. KEYBOARD: ArrowLeft/Right move ±1 byte, ArrowUp/Down move ±bytesPerRow (a 16-byte row jump by default), all clamped to the array bounds. FOOTER: a visible plain-text bar beneath the panes prints, when a range is active, 'selected <n> bytes at 0x<start>–0x<end> · u16=0x<hex> · u32=0x<hex> · utf8="<escaped>"' (u16/u32 little-endian, present only once the range is long enough to fill them; utf8 is a TextDecoder('utf-8',{fatal:false}) best-effort decode of the exact selected bytes, JSON-escaped for control characters); with no range it prints the single hovered/focused byte's offset, hex value and descriptor, or a plain hint at rest. A separate visually-hidden aria-live=polite element (not the visible footer, so it doesn't re-announce on every hover) carries only the short form ('selected 8 bytes at 0x40') and is empty outside a range, so range changes announce without also announcing every hover. A11Y: the hex pane is role=grid with role=gridcell buttons, each named 'offset 0x<idx>, value 0x<byte>, <descriptor>' where descriptor is a control-code mnemonic (NUL, LF, ESC, DEL, ...), the literal printable character, or 'non-ASCII'; the ASCII pane is aria-hidden entirely since it duplicates the grid's information. Colors are token-only (--background/--foreground/--ns-muted/--border via Tailwind utilities, plus the two literal color-mix(var(--foreground)) tints and --ns-accent solely on the focus-visible ring) — no canvas, nothing to re-derive on theme change. No motion beyond a 100-150ms color/opacity transition, skipped under prefers-reduced-motion via motion-reduce:transition-none; there is no rAF loop anywhere in this component.
